title: Projectivity of the unpointed stable coarse moduli scheme
statement: Let $k$ be any field and $g\geq2$. The unpointed stable genus-$g$ moduli groupoid $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,0}$ over $k$, with objects, arrows and coarse-moduli convention as in [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids], is a smooth Deligne--Mumford stack with a finite-type projective coarse moduli $k$-scheme $Q_g$. Projective for $Q_g$ is the finite-projective-space convention [def-kun-projective]. The smooth-family subcategory $\mathcal M_{g,0}$ is a dense open substack. This holds in arbitrary characteristic and without a marking. The field, finite-type and etale notions are [def-weil-field], [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] and [def-weil-etale-morphism].

source.place: Tag 0E9C, theorem-stable-smooth-proper, for the smooth Deligne--Mumford stack and dense smooth locus; projective coarse moduli: D. Mumford, The structure of the moduli spaces of curves and abelian varieties, ICM Nice (1970), printed p.462 (projectivity over Z, joint work with Knudsen and Seshadri). Also de Jong 1996 Section 2.24. Mumford PDF local WANTED; primary author scan read online.

proof.text: The nodal-stack theorem makes $\mathfrak N_k$ algebraic and smooth over $k$. The stable-open theorem identifies our exact scheme/projective-bundle groupoid with its fixed-genus stable open. Restricting the smooth atlas to this open gives algebraicity and smoothness of $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,0}$.

source.place: Tag 0E9C, theorem-stable-smooth-proper, smoothness and DM arguments through 0E79 and 0E7A

proof.text: At a geometric stable $C/\Omega$, take zero markings in the infinitesimal-fields theorem. Stability gives $2g(C_a)-2+\#E_a>0$ on every normalized component: at least three branches in genus zero, at least one in genus one, and positivity in higher genus. Thus infinitesimal automorphisms vanish. The DM-locus criterion's final clause applies to this entire stable open, making it DM in every characteristic.

source.place: Tag 0E9C, theorem-stable-smooth-proper, smoothness and DM arguments through 0E79 and 0E7A

proof.text: The smooth-family theorem supplies the base-change-compatible smooth open. For each geometric stable $C/\Omega$, choose a projective frame of its rank-$19(g-1)$ ten-canonical section space, supplied by the parameter theorem. The existing framed-trait-smoothing theorem gives a stable family over $\Omega[[t]]$ with special fibre $C$ and smooth generic fibre. Apply the trait/chart density lemma to this open: on any etale scheme atlas supplied by step 2 its pullback is dense. Smoothness from step 1 makes this atlas smooth over $k$.

source.place: Tags 0E86 (lemma-smooth-dense), 0E87 (lemma-smooth-dense-in-stable), using examples-defos.tex Tag 0E7Y and curves.tex Tag 0C4E

proof.text: Set $r=19(g-1)\geq19$ and $P(m)=20(g-1)m+1-g$. The parameter theorem supplies projective finite-type $Z$, invariant locally closed $J$ and $G=\operatorname{PGL}_{r,k}$, with the equivalence to our moduli groupoid, preserving all arrows. Its projective-frame torsors are Zariski locally trivial and permit base-line twists.

source.place: Section 3.3, Definition 9, Proposition 10, Corollary 11 and paragraph thereafter; Section 3.4 projectivity, pp.15--18; local PDF WANTED, read online

proof.text: For sufficiently large $m$, Gieseker's theorem supplies an ample $G$-linearized positive Hilbert--Pluecker power $A$ with $J\subset Z^s(A)$ and $J\hookrightarrow Z^{ss}(A)$ closed. These give exactly the stable inclusion and semistable closedness required by the quotient theorem over our arbitrary field; no invertibility of $r$ is assumed.

source.place: Section 3.3, Definition 9, Proposition 10, Corollary 11 and paragraph thereafter; Section 3.4 projectivity, pp.15--18; local PDF WANTED, read online

proof.text: Apply the projective PGL quotient theorem to $(Z,A,J,G)$: step 4 gives projectivity and finite type of $Z$ and $r\geq1$, and step 5 gives its polarized stable closed locus. Obtain finite-type projective $Q_g$ and invariant $q:J\to Q_g$, with algebraic-space universality and geometric orbit bijections. Its Veronese clause gives exactly [def-kun-projective].

source.place: Section 3.3, Definition 9, Proposition 10, Corollary 11 and paragraph thereafter; Section 3.4 projectivity, pp.15--18; local PDF WANTED, read online

proof.text: Use the parameter equivalence of step 4 with the Zariski torsors specified there. The coarse-descent lemma applied to $q$ of step 6 gives $\pi:\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,0}\to h_{Q_g}$. For every algebraic space $B/k$, its invariant-map correspondence and the categorical bijection for $q$ identify maps $Q_g\to B$ with maps $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,0}\to B$. Its geometric-class clause gives the bijection to $Q_g(\Omega)$. These are exactly the current coarse definition for $S=\operatorname{Spec}k$ and zero markings. Steps 1--3 and 6 supply the remaining clauses.

lean.statement: theorem unpointed_stable_coarse_projective (k : Type u) [Field k] (g : ℕ) (hg : 2 ≤ g) : IsDeligneMumfordModuliStack (BasedCategory.ofFunctor (StablePointedModuli.forget (Spec (.of k)) g 0)) ∧ (∃ (Q : Over (Spec (.of k))) (π : BasedFunctor (BasedCategory.ofFunctor (StablePointedModuli.forget (Spec (.of k)) g 0)) (discreteModuli (yoneda.obj Q))), IsCoarseModuliScheme (BasedCategory.ofFunctor (StablePointedModuli.forget (Spec (.of k)) g 0)) Q π ∧ LocallyOfFiniteType Q.hom ∧ QuasiCompact Q.hom ∧ IsHProjective Q.hom) ∧ (∀ X : StablePointedModuli (Spec (.of k)) g 0, ∃ V : X.base.left.Opens, ∀ (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) (b : T ⟶ X.base), Smooth (pullback.snd X.projection b.left) ↔ Set.range b.left ⊆ (V : Set X.base.left)) ∧ (∃ (U : Over (Spec (.of k))) (a : BasedFunctor (discreteModuli (yoneda.obj U)) (BasedCategory.ofFunctor (StablePointedModuli.forget (Spec (.of k)) g 0))), Smooth U.hom ∧ (∀ (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) (t : BasedFunctor (discreteModuli (yoneda.obj T)) (BasedCategory.ofFunctor (StablePointedModuli.forget (Spec (.of k)) g 0))), ∃ (Z : AlgebraicSpace (Spec (.of k))) (p : Z.obj.obj ⟶ yoneda.obj T), HasSpaceBaseChange a T t Z p ∧ SpaceMapIsEtale Z T p ∧ SpaceMapIsSurjective Z T p) ∧ ∃ V : U.left.Opens, Dense (V : Set U.left) ∧ ∀ (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) (b : T ⟶ U), Smooth (a.toFunctor.obj (CostructuredArrow.mk (yoneda.map b))).projection ↔ Set.range b.left ⊆ (V : Set U.left))
